title: Creep-damage material paths and curve projection
purpose: Verify the first release-level local building blocks for high-temperature creep assessment without presenting them as a global finite-element creep solution.
physics: Mises Kachanov-Rabotnov creep damage, hyperbolic-sine creep, and modified-theta curve projection

execution.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_constitutive_models.py -k 'kachanov or theta or sinh'
execution.evidence: Closed-form interval integration, tensor invariants, stress sensitivity, and synthetic-curve recovery are checked independently.

observables: One constant-stress K-R update equals ten subdivided updates.
Associative tensor creep strain is deviatoric and has the requested equivalent increment.
Rupture time decreases as equivalent stress increases.
Modified-theta fitting recovers a known synthetic primary-to-tertiary curve.
Sinh creep rate increases monotonically over the tested positive stress range.
acceptance: Subdivision differences satisfy the automated floating-point tolerances.
Tensor trace and equivalent-strain identities satisfy the automated tolerances.
The fitted projection RMSE is below the declared synthetic-data threshold.
limitations: These are material-point and curve benchmarks, not a global FE benchmark.
The hot-wall example uses illustrative parameters and is not a code-compliance assessment.
Mesh-dependent local damage needs regularization before structural rupture claims.
